Training positive–negative margins are surrogate diagnostics: easy sampled negatives, memorization, or increased score scale can enlarge margins without improving HR@10. Operationally, HR@10 depends on whether at most nine candidates outrank the positive, under the evaluator’s tie rule; mean margins hide this boundary. Track positive ranks and margins against the tenth-highest negative on pinned validation candidates. Sampled HR can reverse full-catalog model comparisons, so interpret results strictly within the unchanged benchmark ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

For comparison, retain paired per-user hit indicators and compute Δ = ¼Σ_category mean(hit_B − hit_A). Recommended uncertainty estimate: a 95% paired bootstrap interval, resampling users within each category while sharing indices across models and preserving candidates. Report category deltas and discordant hit counts; exact McNemar tests suit category-level binary comparisons. Pairing preserves dependence ([SciPy documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). These intervals estimate user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and candidate sets; they exclude training-seed variation, candidate-sampling variation, and adaptive-search selection bias. The fixed benchmark score itself is deterministic.

Mean item cosine cannot establish absence or presence of collapse: opposite directions can cancel despite low rank; a shared mean can raise cosine despite informative variation. Inspect singular spectra of item embeddings and final nonpadding GRU states, excluding padding and using consistent samples. Report centered and uncentered spectra, norms, per-dimension variance, and leading-component energy. RankMe uses exp(−Σpᵢ log pᵢ), with pᵢ = σᵢ/Σσᵢ; distinguish covariance entropy rank, which normalizes σᵢ², and participation ratio, (Σλᵢ)²/Σλᵢ². Flag zero-energy representations explicitly. Effective rank diagnoses dimensional concentration, not guaranteed recommendation quality ([RankMe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02885)).
